portInfo.description: Administración del Sistema Portuario Nacional (ASIPONA) Progreso operates Puerto Progreso on Yucatán’s Gulf coast and publicly discusses cruise passenger movements alongside commercial cargo growth in 2026 notices. A 27 October 2026 headline notes growth in commercial cargo and cruise passengers during 2026, but the captured news page did not yield a usable numeric passenger table in text form. Secondary commercial operators (e.g. SSA Marine México) appear in web indexes as terminal operators; this guide does not promote operator marketing as berth geometry. Until ASIPONA publishes a clear passenger-door plan with coordinates, shore itineraries must treat the landing pin as unverified.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Do not treat Progreso as a “walk straight into town” stop until the day’s shuttle/pier instructions are posted — the passenger door pin remains unverified.
